answer: Reputation Decay Curve. Each agent's standing decays toward a tundra-flat baseline unless refreshed by unique counterparties who themselves hold non-decayed standing. A clone cluster can only refresh itself, so its members' scores stay hollow, and matching weight scales with the square of distinct-origin depth. The anchor for any new identity is a costly cold-start period of near-zero task allocation. An attacker cloning N identities pays N cold-starts plus wasted counterparty diversity that never compounds, making each marginal identity yield diminishing returns.
